title: העצם שבנויה כמו מגדל אייפל
summary: Why the femur is a hollow tube with spongy ends: same material as a rod but far stiffer (Galileo 1638; stiffness ∝ R⁴ − r⁴ vs material ∝ R² − r², ×3.5 at R = 1.5); trabeculae along compression/tension stress lines (Culmann's 'Voilà ma grue!' 1866, von Meyer 1867); Wolff's law (1892) as a feedback loop of bone cells; Koechlin, Culmann's best student, sketched the Eiffel Tower (6 June 1884; 7,300 t iron ≈ 936 m³ ≈ a 6 cm slab on its 125 m base) — the femur-copy story is a myth; hip load ≈ 2.4× body weight; astronauts lose ~1%/month of hip bone; tennis racquet arm +39%; Weizmann's 7 levels of bone.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: lesson runs ~28–33 min (at/just above the 30-min bound); diagonal struts in the Wolff sim stay nearly constant under vertical load
